short: A uniquely designed British supersonic interceptor renowned for its astonishing climb rate and Mach 2 performance.
full:
Entering service with the Royal Air Force in 1959, the English Electric Lightning was designed specifically to defend British airspace against Soviet nuclear bombers. To minimize drag while maximizing power, its two jet engines were uniquely stacked vertically within the fuselage. This gave the Lightning an exceptional thrust-to-weight ratio, allowing it to intercept high-altitude targets at Mach 2 and climb so rapidly it occasionally outpaced the tracking capabilities of early radar systems.

While its performance was legendary, the Lightning was constrained by its specialized interceptor role. Its heavy fuel consumption limited its range and loiter time, and it carried a relatively small weapon payload. It served as Britain's premier front-line fighter throughout the peak of the Cold War before being retired in 1988.
